data.title: Audience Redirected to an Unmoderated Platform
data.summary:
Campaign content directed its audience to platforms with minimal moderation, where the
narrative continues beyond the reach of enforcement and of the organisation's monitoring.
data.description:
Migration is a response to pressure and a sign that enforcement is working, but it
converts a visible problem into an invisible one. The audience that moves is the most
committed portion, and on the destination platform it is exposed to a more extreme version
of the narrative with nothing to moderate it.

For the organisation, monitoring usually stops at the migration point. Judging that the
campaign has ended because activity on mainstream platforms has fallen is a predictable
and costly error.

Collection on these platforms raises its own questions, and the report should set out the
basis on which it was or was not conducted rather than leaving a silent gap.
data.recommendation:
* Continue monitoring after mainstream activity falls; a decline frequently indicates
  migration rather than resolution.
* Establish, with legal, what collection on destination platforms is authorised before it
  is needed.
* Expect the migrated audience to return around trigger events, and watch for it.
data.short_recommendation: Keep monitoring after migration; a quiet mainstream is not resolution.
